title: Tactics transform goals
objective: Before each tactic of a Goal Replay is shown, pick the goal it produces.

choice.prompt: A goal contains `if c then x else y`. After `split`, what is there?

options.why: `split` does not pick a branch for you.

options.text: Two goals: one with `c` as a hypothesis and `x` in place of the `if`, one with `¬c` and `y`
options.why: `split` is a case split on the condition.
`split` divides the work and proves nothing.

options.text: Two goals with no new hypotheses
options.why: Each branch receives its own condition as a hypothesis.

blocks.md:
A tactic is a command that changes the goal. You do not write a proof from its last line backwards: you state the theorem, and each tactic turns the current goal into zero, one or several new ones. The proof ends when no goal is left. To read a proof you track the goal, not the code, and this lesson trains that skill: before each tactic is shown, you predict the goal it produces.

Three tactics carry most ledger proofs. `unfold` replaces a name by its definition. `split` breaks an `if` into two goals, one per branch, each with its branch's condition as a hypothesis. A closing tactic such as `simp` or `omega` finishes the arithmetic. The proof below uses all three on `transferPos_conserves`: after any transfer, the total is unchanged. Every goal in a replay is read from real Lean at build time, through its language server {{run:RUN-lean-plaingoal}}, and never typed by hand.

| Tactic | Turns the goal into |
|---|---|
| `unfold f` | the same goal with `f` replaced by its definition |
| `split` | two goals, one per branch of an `if`, each with its condition in scope |
| `constructor` | one goal for each part of a conjunction |
| `exact t` | no goal at all, if `t` has the goal's type |

Predict the goal after `unfold transferPos total` and make your call. Then step through the rest, predicting each goal before you look.

blocks.direction: Replay shows: the reference proof of `transferPos_conserves`, with the goal before each tactic. Predict the goal, then compare.

code.text:
structure Ledger where
  a : Int
  b : Int
deriving Repr, DecidableEq

def total (s : Ledger) : Int := s.a + s.b

def transferPos (s : Ledger) (n : Int) : Ledger :=
  if 0 < n ∧ n ≤ s.a then { a := s.a - n, b := s.b + n } else s

theorem transferPos_conserves (s : Ledger) (n : Int) :
    total (transferPos s n) = total s := by
  unfold transferPos total
  split <;> simp <;> omega

call.prompt: What will the replay show as the goal after `unfold transferPos total`?

options.text: The `if … then … else …` of `transferPos` now appears inside a sum of fields
options.why: `unfold` replaces both names by their definitions, so the `if` is visible in the goal.
`unfold` rewrites a goal and proves nothing.
Both `transferPos` and `total` occur in the goal, so both are unfolded.

options.text: A new hypothesis `0 < n ∧ n ≤ s.a` appears
options.why: Hypotheses come from case splits, and no split has happened yet.

blocks.after: After `unfold` the goal is still open, now about an `if`. `split` turns that `if` into two cases, and each case receives its condition as a hypothesis. Then `simp` reduces the fields and `omega` finishes the arithmetic {{run:RUN-lean-s2-cells}}. In the lab's manual mode you will write the arithmetic yourself, so notice what `omega` does here.

choice.prompt: `transferKeep s n` is `if 0 < n ∧ n < s.a then { a := s.a - n, b := s.b + n } else s`, so it never empties the sender. The goal is `0 < (transferKeep s n).a`, with `ha : 0 < s.a` in scope. After `unfold transferKeep` and `split`, what is the second goal?

options.text: `ha : 0 < s.a` and `0 < n ∧ n < s.a`; the goal is about the debited balance `s.a - n`
options.why: That is the first goal, the branch where the guard holds.

options.text: `ha : 0 < s.a` only; the goal is `0 < s.a`
options.why: It drops the branch hypothesis. `split` always adds the condition of the branch.

options.text: `ha : 0 < s.a` and `¬(0 < n ∧ n < s.a)`; the goal is `0 < s.a`
options.why: The rejected branch gets the negated guard, and the `if` is replaced by `s`.
`split` divides the work and proves nothing.

choice.prompt: The goal is `0 ≤ (transferPos s n).a ∧ 0 ≤ (transferPos s n).b`, with `ha` and `hb` in scope. After `constructor`, what remains?

options.why: `constructor` splits a conjunction into its two parts.

options.text: Two goals, one for each part, and `ha` and `hb` are used up
options.why: Hypotheses are not consumed. Both goals still have `ha` and `hb`.

options.text: No goals, because the facts in scope already close it
options.why: Closing a goal takes `exact` or another tactic. `constructor` only splits.

options.text: Two goals, `0 ≤ (transferPos s n).a` and `0 ≤ (transferPos s n).b`, each with `ha` and `hb` in scope
options.why: A conjunction is proved by proving both parts, and the hypotheses stay in scope.

notes: Re-run by W0-S11 from research/evidence/A5r3/scripts/lean-plaingoal.mjs (spine section 9.5). The one change: the script's docker run gains --memory=6g, the cap every container on this host runs with; the input "as run" is that copy.

Recorded for W1 follow-up 1 (docs/waves/W1-report.md). run@1's task field admits only W<n>-S<nn>/W<n>-T<nn> IDs, so the follow-up is named in task_label instead.

Each log is the container's stdout and stderr, as lean printed them. verdict_lines are the error and warning header lines, the #print axioms lines and the #eval/#check output lines, copied from the log.

Lesson cells are copied verbatim from the lesson named in each configuration's inputs. Where a cell uses definitions from an earlier cell of the lesson (or, for S2.L7, from S2.L3's cell, whose Ledger, total and transferPos S2.L7 relies on), those lines precede it in the input file.

Configurations named probe-* are not lesson code: the lessons and drawers cite a message or an axiom list without giving the code, so a minimal file was written to produce it. Their inputs are committed beside the others.

The cell in S2.L5 cell 3 is a claim card for `statespace check`'s claim@1 validation; the bench's statespace CLI has no claim-card validator (its check command runs lab stages), so that cell is not recorded here.
D-07's deprecation exhibit uses Int.ofNat_nonneg, one of the names Lean 4.35.0's core marks deprecated.
